business_scope.primary_industry_name: Statutory Company Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Office

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (single national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified private law; Commercial Code; administrative law separated under dual-court system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 30 May 1984, amended by 2013 Protocol)
France–Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Agreement (2010, as amended by 2017 Protocol)
France–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended)
France–Switzerland Double Taxation Agreement (1966, as amended)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union – Articles 49–55 (Freedom of Establishment)
General Agreement on Trade in Services (WTO/GATS) – commercial presence commitments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L561-1 et seq. and R561-1 et seq.; Code de commerce Articles L561-2-2 and R561-1 to R561-7 (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE); Ordonnance n°2016-1635 and Décret n°2018-284 (UBO transparency); Loi n°2020-1508 (trust and corporate transparency); Regulation (EU) 2015/847 (funds transfer information); TRACFIN procedural guidelines under CMF R561-23.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified full-color copy of valid passport of each UBO, shareholder and statutory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of each individual's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if origin is a 1961 Hague Convention state) or Consular Legalization of the French Embassy/Consulate (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / register extract of any foreign corporate shareholder (original or certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing issued within the last 90 days for any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or competent government authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential/professional address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or licensed bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of every non-French document listed above
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Expert translator certified by a French Cour d'Appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; translator's certification affixed and signed before a French authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of each UBO and director against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (FSF), and French domestic freezing decisions (Ministry of Economy – Direction générale du Trésor) at origination and on a continuous 24/7 basis; Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status determined in accordance with CMF R561-18-1 (family members and known close associates included); enhanced due diligence and TRACFIN suspicious transaction reporting triggered on any PEP match, negative news indicator, or unexplained source of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique Électronique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated with the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) for the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS); name availability search via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings must be in French (Loi Toubon n°94-665); the legal name may contain foreign words but must be rendered in Latin script and be lawfully transcribed in the French corporate documents; any foreign-language designation used in contracts, commercial offers or employment documents must be accompanied by an equally binding French version; French-only jurisdiction: no Cyrillic, Arabic or CJK script entries are admissible in the RCS register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, établissement de crédit, société de financement
Caisse des Dépôts, Bourse de Paris, AFNOR, CROUS
Any token falsely suggesting a regulated or public authority status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France applies no formal pre-registration name reservation; distinctiveness is assessed at the moment of the RCS filing. Upon rejection by the INPI/Registry (e.g., identity with a prior trade name, protected mark, or public-order contrariety), the applicant may apply for judicial relief by way of urgent application (référé) before the Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office location within 15 days of notification, or file a fresh application with a modified name. Tokens classified as sensitive require ex ante written authorization from the competent supervisory authority (e.g., ACPR for 'Banque'/'Assurance'); refusal of such authorization is appealable to the administrative court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted exclusively through a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) holding prior ministerial approval (agrément) under Article R123-166-2 of the Code de commerce; the domiciliation contract must evidence genuine client allocation of the address and postal handling; a fully virtual set-up without any employment, revenue or operational substance in France will be challenged by TRACFIN and tax auditors.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-moderate (quantified likelihood 15–25% during the first 24 months for a registered-agent and corporate-secretarial operator classified as 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced'; unannounced physical inspections may be conducted under CMF R561-23 by TRACFIN and by the social/tax inspectorates for payroll or premises substance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SAS drafting with cross-border shareholders (USD 2,500–3,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal notice (avis de constitution) in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) of the registered-office department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Publisher authorized by the Prefecture of the department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per insertion line fixed by arrêté préfectoral

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consolidated incorporation filing fee (immatriculation au RCS) paid through the Guichet Unique Électronique (INPI fee + fixed duties)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff published by INPI (currently EUR ~65–75)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial domiciliation (registered office) agreement – first quarterly fee with licensed domiciliation company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed société de domiciliation (holding agrément R123-166-2)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (EUR 30–120 per month dependent on city and services)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC pre-incorporation due-diligence file and UBO register preparation (RBE filing) by compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Medium_Risk_Enhanced client profile (USD 1,200–2,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation of foreign UBO and corporate-shareholder documents (approx. 7 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Expert translator certified by a French Cour d'Appel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization fees for foreign-origin documents (passport, certificate of incorporation, good standing, proof of address – estimated 4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authority (apostille) or French Consulate (consular legalization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention per-document fee schedules / French consular tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for ISIC 8299 corporate-secretarial service providers (USD 3,000–5,000 first year)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-29 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) and Articles R.224-1 to R.227-31; supplemented by Décret n°84-406 (company registry formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registry) within the jurisdiction of the registered office; online through the Infogreffe/Guichet unique electronic portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 form (déclaration de création de société) plus notarized or privately signed Articles of Association (statuts), submitted via the Guichet Unique des Formalités Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under French law for SAS; articles may set capital as low as €1, but any cash contribution must be fully subscribed and deposited into a French bank account or with a notary/Caisse des Dépôts before registration, blocked until certificate of incorporation is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOCIÉTÉ PAR ACTIONS SIMPLIFIÉE. On this day, the founder unanimously: (1) acknowledges full subscription and release of the share capital as set out in the Articles; (2) confirms the registered office address at [●], France; (3) adopts the proposed corporate objects covering registered-agent and secretarial services; (4) appoints [Name] as President, [Name] as General Manager, and mandates the President to represent the company before the Commercial Registry and to sign all filings, including the M0 declaration, and to open a bank account for the company. This resolution is effective immediately until amended by a corporate deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or bank of the company (upon selection of registered office location)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft French-language Articles of Association (statuts) complying with Articles L.227-1 to L.227-29. Open a temporary capital contribution account with a bank or notary and deposit at least the full amount of the subscribed cash capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage).
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all shareholders and officers
Proof of availability of company name (certificat de non-concurrence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Articles are ambiguous or incomplete, revise clauses and re-execute; if deposit certificate is rejected, rectify bank account references.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via Infogreffe and the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the French national trade register (RCS) for identical or confusingly similar names. Reserve the desired corporate name through the Guichet Unique by submitting the name request and obtaining a certificate of non-opposition.
required_dossiers: Potential signatories' authority to bind the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refusal due to prior mark, submit a revised name or file opposition/time-limit response through INPI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Signature of Articles and appointment of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute final Articles of Association before a notary if signatures are certified, or by private deed. Include appointment clauses naming the President and any Directors General. Ensure all shares are subscribed and paid in accordance with the blocking certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If signature formalities incomplete, obtain corrected signatures and re-notarize. If a shareholder objects, execute a separate deed of appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publication of the company formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official legal announcement journal (JAL - Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the mandatory legal notice in a French legal gazette (JAL) in the jurisdiction of the registered office. Include company name, legal form, share capital, address, president's name, and company object. Obtain proof of publication (attestation de parution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is rejected for missing data, promptly amend notice and resubmit; extension of SLA typical.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing M0 application with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités Entreprises (operated by INPI) serving the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the M0 form online or via the CFE. Upload the Articles, legal publication notice, capital blocking certificate, and officer identity documents. Pay the registry fee electronically. Receive a filing receipt and registration number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of non-opposition for the company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query, respond within the prescribed deadline (usually 15 days) by submitting corrective documents; failure can result in dismissal of the application, requiring a new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the registry issues the K-bis extract (registre du commerce et des sociétés). Obtain the SIREN number, SIRET number, and NAF code (8299Z for secretarial services). Register with URSSAF (social contributions) and the tax administration for VAT and corporate income tax.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If K-bis incorrect, request administrative correction to the Greffe; if tax registration delayed, file a direct rectification request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture du département (Departmental Prefecture) — Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail, des Solidarités et de la Protection des Populations (DDETS-PP) for service enterprise licensing; Bureau de la Domiciliation for commercial registered-office providers.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aggrément de domiciliation d'entreprise (Commercial Domiciliation Agreement Licence) — required if the SAS provides registered-office/company-secretarial premises; otherwise a business registration suffices under the Code de commerce.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based secretarial and domiciliation services fall outside the classified installation (ICPE) regime and do not require either an EIA report or an environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from office premises must comply with municipal sewer discharge authorization and the French Public Health Code (Code de la santé publique) hygiene rules; waste handling must follow the waste sorting and classification provisions of the Environmental Code (Articles R.541-1 et seq.), particularly for paper and electronic archives. No VOC or atmospheric discharge thresholds apply unless backup diesel generators are installed, in which case the threshold in the ICPE rubrique 2910 applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued after a commission control visit (Permis de feu / attestation de sécurité) under the Code de la construction et de l'habitation if the premises host more than 30 persons or are open to the public; structural load inspection by a certified office for archive areas; workplace clearance and professional risk assessment (DUERP) issued by the employer in association with the état des servitudes and an occupational health check by the services de prévention et de santé au travail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), under the Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. The principal online portal is impots.gouv.fr. Business tax matters are generally handled by the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); non-established businesses requiring French VAT registration are generally handled by the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the competent Centre de formalités des entreprises/Guichet unique operated by INPI. Following registration in the Registre national des entreprises and, where applicable, the Registre du commerce et des sociétés, it receives a SIREN identifier and establishment-level SIRET identifiers; the SIREN is used as the basis of its French business tax identification. The company must separately activate its professional account on impots.gouv.fr and complete applicable corporate income tax, payroll, and other tax registrations. A French VAT number is obtained from the competent tax office and follows the format FR plus a two-character key and the company's nine-digit SIREN. A foreign company making French taxable supplies that require registration should apply to the SIEE before commencing those supplies, providing evidence of legal existence, business activity, and the identity and authority of its representative. A business established outside the EU generally must appoint a French VAT representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or other statutory exception removes that requirement. Registration thresholds or small-business exemption rules do not generally excuse a non-established supplier from registration where its French transactions are taxable and no special rule applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS); France does not provide a general US-style check-the-box election. A qualifying newly formed, non-listed company may elect temporary partnership-style taxation under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code for up to five fiscal years, subject to statutory conditions including qualifying ownership, employee and turnover or balance-sheet criteria and restrictions on its principal activity. Certain qualifying family companies may elect partnership taxation under separate rules. These are limited statutory elections, not general hybrid-mismatch elections. French anti-hybrid rules implement applicable EU and OECD measures and do not create an elective entity-classification regime. The standard IS rate is 25%; a qualifying small company may benefit from the 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, the domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) is subject to statutory turnover limits, generally EUR 37,500 for services and EUR 85,000 for goods for 2025, with higher tolerance limits of EUR 41,250 and EUR 93,500, respectively, subject to applicable rules and legislative changes. These are exemption limits, not a general registration threshold for foreign businesses. A non-established business making French transactions for which it is liable to account for French VAT generally must register from the first such transaction; no general turnover threshold applies. Cross-border EU small-enterprise relief may be available only if its specific conditions and notification requirements are met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not generally require prior real-time clearance of domestic VAT invoices. Under the phased domestic e-invoicing reform, all businesses within scope must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations are scheduled from that date for large and intermediate-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. In-scope transactions are to be transmitted through an approved platform (plateforme agréée) and the central directory; transaction and payment data reporting (e-reporting) applies to specified transactions outside domestic e-invoicing, including relevant cross-border and consumer transactions. Foreign suppliers' obligations depend on establishment, transaction type, and the statutory scope of the reform. There is no general VAT digital stamp or universal real-time invoice-clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the EU to a destination outside the EU may be exempt from French VAT with deduction rights, subject to the statutory conditions and reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. Intra-EU supplies are generally exempt with deduction rights only when the customer and reporting conditions are met; they are not exports outside the EU. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer or supplier is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies, including the general B2B rule and its exceptions. For a French taxable person exporting goods or supplying qualifying services, input VAT recovery requires valid invoices, a business-purpose link, and compliance with reporting and evidentiary requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and customs exit results or equivalent evidence confirming exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, sales contract, packing list, and transport documents appropriate to the shipment, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, or CMR
Proof of delivery or receipt by the customer where available
Proof of payment and accounting records linking the payment to the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite
For services, contract, invoices, evidence of the customer's business status and location where relevant, and records supporting the applicable place-of-supply treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export exemption claims may be denied or clawed back if exit from the EU or other statutory conditions are not substantiated, with output VAT, interest for late payment, and applicable tax penalties assessed. Depending on the circumstances, penalties may include the general 10% late-payment surcharge, increased surcharges for non-compliance after formal notice, and penalties of 40% for deliberate breaches or 80% for specified fraudulent or abusive conduct; criminal prosecution may apply to serious tax fraud. The exact assessment depends on the facts, applicable procedural rules, and the taxpayer's conduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), acting as macro-prudential supervisor, balance-of-payments registrar, and holder of the CPSS/EPB reporting gateway; enforcement of the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF) is shared with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking conduct and with the Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) for capital-market FX instruments; external financial regulatory guidance sits with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Relance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the euro on both current-account and capital-account basis under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Article L151-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code; France applies no exchange-control authorization system for ordinary business transactions, no parallel exchange market, and no repatriation or earmarking requirement on inbound or outbound payments; the SAS is free to hold multi-currency accounts, to remit dividends and management fees to non-resident shareholders without advance approval, and to settle cross-border service fees in any freely convertible currency; limited residual screening applies under the foreign direct investment (FDI) prior-authorization regime for sensitive sectors in Article L151-3 CMF, but ISIC 8299 registered-agent services are outside the strategic list; banking counterparties nevertheless enforce EU/OECD/OFAC sanctions and ACPR liquidity requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Neither France nor the euro area imposes a mandatory export-proceeds surrender obligation or a forced conversion ratio; a French SAS may lawfully retain 100% of export and service-proceeds in a foreign-currency account held at a French or foreign credit institution; however, resident companies must file the statistical balance-of-payments declarations ('déclaration de change') with Banque de France when cumulative gross flows cross the de minimis threshold of EUR 15 million per calendar year, using the BP-OVP limited portal; individual cross-border transfers exceeding EUR 10,000 in cash require customs declaration under Article L152-1 CMF; corporate retention of receivables abroad must be evidenced by the commercial contract, the export invoice, and the bank SWIFT reference (MT103), with records kept for 10 years for tax and customs verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability with strict limitations: ACPR-licensed or PSD2-passporting payment institutions and electronic money institutions (notably Qonto, Payplug, and Shine) can technically onboard the French SAS remotely and provide fast, low-cost EUR collecting accounts and card-acceptance rails, but they cannot issue the 'attestation de dépôt de fonds' required for capital formation on a 'compte bloqué' unless they hold a full credit-institution license, nor do they provide reliable SWIFT correspondent clearing into Asia, the Gulf, or North America; moreover, for ISIC 8299 (TCSP-type registered-agent services), the AML/CFT classification mandates an account held at a licensed credit institution to validate the ACPR and Guichet-TCSP compliance relationship; therefore the blueprint requires the primary treasury account at a Tier-1 bank, with fintech/EMI accounts used only as secondary collection tunnels capped at 25% of monthly inflows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted in France under the Fifth AML Directive and eIDAS and through ACPR-recognised video-identity providers, and most Tier-1 banks accept video KYC for non-PEP, non-sanctioned shareholders; however, in practice, for a company flagged as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under the TCSP classification, French core banks require one physical appearance of the legal representative at the branch (or before a bank-designated notaire), apostilled and certified translations of all constitutional documents of the SAS and of its non-EU ultimate shareholders, and a signed compliance interview with the 'Responsable LCB-FT' (AML compliance officer); the physical-presence mandate can be waived only if the SAS is introduced via a recognized registered-agent network with a pre-existing correspondent relationship, in which case the bank performs a 'visio-conference de conformité' recorded for audit; the KYC package must be completed within five business days and refreshed periodically.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector rejection: 'Registered Agent and Offshore Secretarial Services' is classified as a Trust and Company Service Provider (TCSP) under Article L561-2(3°) CMF; the bank refuses account opening until the TCSP authorization or registration evidence is produced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) the Guichet TCSP registration receipt issued by the Ministère de l'Intérieur; (ii) the current extrait Kbis from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés showing the corporate-object clause for statutory secretarial services; (iii) certificate of professional indemnity insurance (RC professionnelle); (iv) declaration of the beneficial-owner register (RBE) filed with INPI listing all UBOs; (v) a copy of the FinCEN/CRS registration number; (vi) a written AML/CFT compliance manual containing the entity's risk map ('cartographie des risques') prepared under Article R561-12 CMF; and (vii) the nom-card of the designated AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity and high-risk residency: ultimate shareholders are domiciled in non-FATF-compliant or grey-listed jurisdictions, or the corporate chain contains bearer-share vehicles or trusts that prevent identification of the true beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) a complete UBO structure chart certified by the legal representative; (ii) apostilled and translated certificate of incorporation and register of members of each intermediate holding; (iii) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for the capital injection; (iv) audited financial statements of intermediate entities for the last two years, where available; (v) FATCA/CRS self-certification forms (Formulaire 5000) for each UBO; (vi) independent World-Check/Dow Jones negative-news report on each UBO; and (vii) an undertaking not to onboard clients resident in sanctioned or non-cooperative jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening: results of the names-screening process generate a potential match on a politically exposed person, a designated terrorist, or an OFAC/EU-sanctioned entity due to the general nature of offshore secretarial services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) the bank's own enhanced-due-diligence questionnaire completed with the exact relationship to the matched person; (ii) a clear-source-of-funds presentation showing that no sanctioned funds ever touch the French SAS accounts; (iii) sworn declarations from UBOs that they are not entities subject to EU/OFAC asset freezes; (iv) engagement letters or client contracts demonstrating lawful corporate administration only (no nominee-ever tasks); (v) client-jurisdiction risk classification in line with FATF mutual evaluations; and (vi) consent to an audit clause permitting the bank to inspect the full client register on demand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-profile mismatch: 'Tributary income via credit card' is expected while the business model is labeled as discretionary corporate services; the bank flags the account as potentially a payment-acceptance or money-mule conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply: (i) a sample of executed client service agreements describing the specific annual registered-agent deliverables and renewal schedules; (ii) a fee schedule mapping card payments to identifiable deliverables (e.g., 350 EUR per yearly secretarial filing); (iii) a six-month projected cash-flow model showing that card inflows will remain below 25% of total receipts; (iv) a statement confirming that no third-party payment-processing, no escrow, and no money-transfer services are offered; (v) evidence of PCI-DSS compliance for any payment page; and (vi) an undertaking to route all one-off large transactions above EUR 10,000 exclusively by bank wire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for share capital and shareholder loans: non-resident shareholders transmit an MT103/SEPA transfer to the French SAS iban at the selected Tier-1 bank using remittance information 'Apport de capital SAS [NAME] - fonds de roulement', together with the share-subscription agreement and a sworn declaration of non-resident status; for third-party client receipts, a credit-card acquiring contract with an authorized PSP is permitted, while institutional clients should pay by wire referencing the invoice number; the bank requests the Banque de France purpose/statistical codes: for equity capital, code 'IF.31' (investissement direct - capital), and for service exports, code 'IC.11' or 'IC.12' as mapped by the balance-of-payments annex; on arrival of the capital the bank executes the 'attestation de dépôt de fonds' for the notaire or the CFE/INPI guichet, and in accordance with Article L227-2 CMF the funds remain blocked for five days where a single shareholder has contributed all assets; the account committee performs a final name-screening before any treasury sweeps, and non-EU inbound wires above EUR 50,000 are reported by the bank to Banque de France through the balance-of-payments (BP) reporting platform.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: intra-EEA supplier payments are executed by SEPA Credit Transfer, optionally via SEPA Instant (up to EUR 100,000 per transaction); all non-EEA statutory filing fees, registered-agent renewals, and professional legal fees are settled by SWIFT MT103 with full structured remittance information; for significant USD flows above EUR 100,000, the correspondent bank clearing runs via CHIPS/FedWire through the Paris bank's New York correspondent with a mandatory 6-character purpose code and interbank reference (MT202 optional); documentary commercial letters of credit are permitted only where physical registry documents or notarized packages are exported as goods; for a pure services business model the recommended method is a 30-60 day sight draft under a confirmed irrevocable L/C issued by the French bank, although most treasury flows should prefer open-account arrangements; all outgoing payments require internal 'four-eyes' validation, and beneficiary accounts in foreign currencies are converted at the bank's closing spot rate with the value date shown on the FX confirmation ticket.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot Contracts (change au comptant) for immediate settlement of trade and capital flows
FX Forward Contracts (change à terme) up to 24 months with no upfront premium, executed under ISDA or French CMF master agreement to hedge forecasted USD/GBP/CHF cash flows

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exposures in non-convertible currencies such as CNY, KRW, INR, MYR, or BRL, with reference to a published WM/Reuters fixing, permitted exclusively for hedging the SAS commercial flows
FX Swaps (swap de change) combining spot and forward legs for treasury liquidity management without modifying the underlying exposure
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCIRS) for long-term alignment of USD receivables with EUR funding liabilities, tenor 1-5 years
FX Options (options de change), including European-style calls and puts and zero-premium collars, subject to ACPR suitability and margin rules
Listed EUR/USD and EUR/GBP futures cleared through EU CCPs (Eurex or ICE) for granular daily hedging of net positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of SAS annual accounts by the sole shareholder or shareholders (approbation des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records / minute book of the SAS; the signed approval minutes are retained on-site but are not filed with a regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal-year end; for a 31 December year-end, shareholder approval must occur by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure of the SAS president to submit the annual accounts to shareholder approval is punishable by a fine of up to €9,000; the Tribunal de Commerce may appoint a court agent to convene the shareholders' meeting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annexes, management report) with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court), submitted electronically through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; for a 31 December year-end, the hard filing deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing is subject to fines up to €1,500 for small companies and up to €4,500 for larger entities; the court may order the filing within a set period under an astreinte (periodic penalty payment), and persistent non-compliance may trigger prosecution of the legal representative

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration and balance payment (déclaration de résultat, Form 2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French corporate taxpayer account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal-year end; for a 31 December year-end, the e-filed return is due by 30 April, with the electronic filing window extending to 3 May for December closers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% tax increase if settled within 30 days of the statutory due date, 40% thereafter, plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; wilful non-filing may attract criminal sanctions and re-assessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner (UBO) declaration update and annual consistency check
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court), submitted electronically through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in direct or indirect ownership or control of the SAS; there is no fixed annual filing date, but the declaration must be re-verified when the annual accounts are deposited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the beneficial-owner declaration is punishable by a fine of up to €15,000 under the Monetary and Financial Code, and the registry may refuse subsequent filings until the declaration is rectified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution return and payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises — CFE), if the SAS holds premises or a place of business in France
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the registered office location
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return filed in the first five months of the calendar year for premises held on 1 January; assessed amounts are billed in the autumn and payable in November of the same tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 10% penalty plus late-payment interest; late payment triggers enforcement proceedings by DGFiP and may oblige the company to pre-pay following-year contributions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at fiscal-year end, it exceeds two of the three thresholds: balance sheet total above €4,000,000, net turnover above €8,000,000 and average permanent workforce above 50 employees; audit is also mandatory for SAS heading a group or when the articles of association or a shareholder request a court-appointed auditor, while small SAS below the thresholds remain exempt
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (ANC Regulation 2014-03, Plan Comptable Général) for SAS statutory accounts; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements and is mandatory for EU-listed groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not apply a fixed annual UBO filing date; the registered agent must submit an updated beneficial-owner declaration to the RCS within 30 days of every share transfer, ownership or control change and must re-certify the declaration at the time of each annual accounts deposit. Each SAS share transfer must be recorded in the register of securities movements, with date, number of shares transferred, par value, parties and book-entry effect stated, and must be consistent with the declared beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Securities Movements / Share Transfers (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Corporate Decisions / Shareholders' Minutes (Registre des décisions)
Beneficial-Owner Declaration compliance copy (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, filed with RCS with on-site copy retained)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: €600 – €2,200 per year (approx. $650 – $2,400) for a French registered office address plus professional corporate secretarial agent support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €5,000 – €15,000 (approx. $5,400 – $16,200) for a standard SAS statutory audit without group consolidation; fees increase for consolidated statements, internal-control reports or court-ordered special audits

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits, apprenticeship tax credit, innovation status deductions, and temporary tax holidays for qualifying investments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 1200 - Déclaration de résultat, submitted electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after adjustments for permanent establishment and French-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only income attributable to a French permanent establishment; foreign-source income generally exempt

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for operating expenses, depreciation, and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to expenses incurred in France or attributable to French PE; foreign tax credits claimed where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation and payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment due within the same deadline as filing; interest accrues on late payments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Administrative fine of €250 minimum to €75,000 maximum plus 0.5% of the tax due per month of delay up to a maximum of 5%, plus possible criminal sanctions for fraudulent filings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no withholding tax on dividends distributed by French companies)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply Double Tax Treaty benefits via submission of TRC (Taxation des Revenus de l'Etranger) form to French tax authorities with supporting documentation; claim reduced rates or exemptions where treaty provisions apply
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% to 25% statutory rate, reduced by applicable treaties (often 0-10%); Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced by treaties to 0-10% depending on recipient status and treaty

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated group turnover for local file and master file requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations require demonstration of adequate physical presence, core income-generating activities, and qualified employees for certain activities to prevent artificial tax avoidance structures

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of Déclaration de résultat within the three-month deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of €250 to €75,000 plus 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (maximum 5%), plus interest on unpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal restitution obligations for unpaid taxes; potential disqualification from office and criminal prosecution for repeated or fraudulent non-filing

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or issuance of false financial statements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 500% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to five years, and confiscation of illicit gains
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil leading to personal civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain arm's-length transfer pricing documentation or application of non-arm's-length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 500% of the tax adjustment plus interest and possible restitution of tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal financial liability for restitution and potential criminal sanctions if intent to evade is proven
